title: B1 fix round: codex_available(complexity) and a mirroring legacy sync (review T-0021 request_changes)
spec:
Why: review T-0021 (sonnet, account B) on B1 commit 361b7ce returned request_changes. Full comment text: read /Users/k3ntaw/code/orchestrator/.orchestrator/tasks/T-0021.json (result.comments). Summary:
- HIGH pool.py:~213 — codex_available() probes pick_executor("execute", 1): returns True when any codex executor has headroom at complexity 1, even if the task's real complexity has no eligible executor (e.g. complexity 8 with astra out of budget but luna/terra/sol free). Also the provider check is trivially true because every row is codex.
- MED pool.py:~204 — _sync_legacy_codex folds self.codex.running/day_tasks into the matched row with max() only, never assigning down. executor.py builds a fresh Pool() per call, so after executor._run decrements pool.codex.running the row keeps the old maximum; running ratchets up to max_parallel and the executor looks permanently busy.

What (2 files: orchestrator/pool.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py; this worktree branches from task/T-0016 so B1's code is present):
1. `codex_available(self, complexity: int = 1) -> bool`: return True iff pick_executor("execute", complexity) is not None. Keep the default so existing callers (mcp.status, cli, executor.start until B2) work; document that B2 must pass the task's complexity. Drop the redundant provider filter or make it meaningful (provider == "codex" of the returned executor only).
2. `_sync_legacy_codex`: mirror, do not max: set the matched row's running = self.codex.running and day_tasks = max(row.day_tasks, self.codex.day_tasks) only when the day matches (day_tasks is monotonic within a day, running is not). Cooldown: row.cooldown_until = max(row.cooldown_until, self.codex.cooldown_until) and apply the group cooldown when the legacy value is in the future. Add a docstring line saying this bridge is removed by B2.
3. Tests (class Executors): (a) astra.day_tasks = astra.daily_budget_tasks → codex_available(8) is False while codex_available(3) is True; (b) legacy sync: set pool.codex.running = 2, save, new Pool() shows astra.running == 2; then pool.codex.running = 0, save, new Pool() shows astra.running == 0 (ratchet regression test); (c) existing Executors tests still pass.

Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py`. Commit: "pool: codex_available takes complexity; legacy codex sync mirrors running instead of ratcheting (review T-0021)" with a revert-path body.
acceptance: uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py exits 0 with the two new regression tests
Pool().codex_available(8) is False when astra is over budget and the 1–6 executors are free
running count on the astra row follows pool.codex.running down as well as up across fresh Pool() instances
git diff --stat limited to orchestrator/pool.py and tests/test_orchestrator.py

result.summary:
Committed at `5cc7d0b`. All green.

**Summary:** Fixed T-0021's two review findings in `orchestrator/pool.py`:
1. `codex_available()` now takes a `complexity` param (default 1) and checks `pick_executor("execute", complexity)` against the real band instead of always probing complexity 1, so a busy/exhausted high-complexity executor (astra) is no longer masked by idle low-band ones (luna/terra/sol).
2. `_sync_legacy_codex` now mirrors `running` directly instead of `max()`-ing it, fixing the ratchet where `executor.py`'s per-call fresh `Pool()` could never bring the row's `running` back down. `day_tasks` stays maxed within the same day (still monotonic there).

**Files changed:** `orchestrator/pool.py`, `tests/test_orchestrator.py` (matches scope exactly).

**Test output:** `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py` — 30 tests, all pass, no failures. New regression tests `test_codex_available_respects_complexity` and `test_legacy_running_syncs_down_not_just_up` both pass. `tests_green.sh` gate also exits 0.
